trust_decision.summary: Before each call_aws command runs, call_aws_helper decides whether the user's denylist/elicitList and read-only policy allow it. At the pinned commit the server starts anyway when the read-only operations index fails to load (READ_OPERATIONS_INDEX=None), and the None branch then skips check_security_policy (and with it the denylist).

landing_point.why: The summary says 'startup initialization failure'. main()'s try/except around get_read_only_operations() logs a warning and sets the index to None.

fix_sites.module_kind: request handler (same file as landing point)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both fix hunks are in server.py (fix.diff:47-87, fix.diff:91-106). No second implementation reaches interpret_command or execute_awscli_customization; call_aws_helper's only caller is server.py:278.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 policy-file route: the project's own test says a malformed or unreadable user policy file 'should be handled gracefully' with an empty denylist (src/aws-api-mcp-server/tests/test_security_policy.py:105-138). A solver can argue it is a user config error, not the transient startup/network failure the advisory describes, and that changing it breaks an existing test.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: No policy file is a supported default: the server warns and applies no extra policy. A fix that treats a missing file like a broken one, or denies whenever the denylist is empty, breaks normal use. Read-only mode and mutation consent must keep working while the index is present.

O6_input_shapes: list of commands in batch mode (server.py:255-270)
--region * wildcard expanded into several commands before the helper (core/aws/service.py:286-294)

O7_producer.where: src/aws-api-mcp-server/awslabs/aws_api_mcp_server/core/metadata/read_only_operations_list.py:143-145 (get_read_only_operations, network fetch at :54); also SecurityPolicy._load_policy at src/aws-api-mcp-server/awslabs/aws_api_mcp_server/core/security/policy.py:56-87

O8_uncovered_routes.route: An unreadable or malformed ~/.aws/aws-api-mcp/mcp-security-policy.json is caught and logged, leaving denylist/elicitList empty, and the command is allowed. The policy is reloaded on every request (service.py:100), so a file broken mid-run fails open too.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: An existing project test asserts this graceful empty-policy behaviour (tests/test_security_policy.py:105-138), and it is user config, not the startup index failure the advisory names.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (core/security) from server.py; one call deep via core/aws/service.py:100

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The per-service lazy fetch could swallow its network error and cache an empty or permissive list instead of raising.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The constructor already swallows errors in a sibling style (lines 53-57 log first). A maintainer wanting resilience to transient servicereference outages could easily write try/except-and-continue here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The customizations loader could log and continue instead of re-raising, so composite commands (s3 cp, etc.) skip the checks on their underlying API calls.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It sits right under _load_policy, which already logs and continues. Making both loaders consistent is a natural refactor.

O9_family: fail-open on initialization failure (CWE-455/CWE-636): security policy skipped when enforcement data fails to load

O10_build.project_tests: src/aws-api-mcp-server/tests/test_server.py, tests/test_security_policy.py (mock the network index fetch and the AWS calls)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Make main() re-raise on index load failure and leave call_aws_helper's None branch (read-only/consent-only fallback, no denylist) in place, or keep a None fallback that still skips the denylist.

out_of_scope_notes: expand_regions_if_needed calls get_active_regions (an AWS call) before any policy check (server.py:265, core/aws/service.py:293). It is server-initiated and read-only; not pursued.
When no policy file exists, _load_policy returns before _load_customizations (core/security/policy.py:60-65), so the customization mapping is never loaded; not pursued.
